newsitem.title: USA: Daxor halts sperm collections after ruling.
newsitem.headline: Daxor halts sperm collections after ruling.

text.p: Daxor Corp said Monday that New York state officials on June 6 had ordered its unit IDANT Laboratories to halt collections of sperm, blood and tissue as a result of a court order from the New York State Court of Appeals.

The company said disruptions of its laboratory in New York's Empire State Building, which it described as the only accredited semen bank in the state, would have a moderately negative impact on company income.

It said the Court of Appeals, the state's highest court, informed the company June 6 it had overturned a ruling made May 31, 1996 by the Appellate Division of New York State Supreme Court which had allowed to company to operate without a license from the New York State Department of Health.

Dr. Joseph Feldschuh, chief executive officer of Daxor, said the 1996 lower court decision came after the company disputed a ruling by the health department of alleged violations and deficiencies at its laboratory.

Feldschuh told Reuters the earlier ruling, in effect, gave the company time to seek further review of the health department refusal to grant it a state license based on the alleged violations. But he said no such hearings had been given.
He sharply criticized the Court of Appeals ruling.
"They mentioned in the ruling we are not entitled to a hearing on the violations and deficiencies," Feldschuh said, adding he believed the refusal violated the company's constitutional rights.
He added Daxor was considering appealing the ruling, either by asking to reargue the case before the Court of Appeals or by appealing to the U.S. Supreme Court.
